problem_statement: hymhub/css-to-tailwind is a runnable Next.js developer tool that translates raw CSS into Tailwind utility classes in a two-pane workspace: a live CSS editor on one side and an 'Out Code' translator pane on the other, with a SetConfig popover (prefix / useAllDefaultValues / customTheme), a light/dark theme toggle, per-rule Copy buttons and a GitHub link, all served under the /css-to-tailwind basePath. The output pane now offers a native utility-CATEGORY filter over the emitted 'Out Code' rules: a 'Filter utilities' tab row (All / Layout / Spacing / Color / Effects) with a live 'Showing N of M utilities' readout, so a developer migrating a large stylesheet can scan just the spacing or colour utilities. The current build of this filter is broken three ways: (1) the tab row is laid out as a fixed non-wrapping 540-640px flex row, so on a 390px phone it juts hundreds of pixels past the viewport and drags the whole converter workspace into a horizontal scroll; (2) the emitted utility chips are shingled with negative margins over a near-identical dark colour, so the converted classes collapse into an illegible dark-on-dark smear; (3) the filter's active-tab marker and its 'Showing N of M utilities · <category>' readout are frozen — clicking a category re-filters the chips but the highlighted tab and the readout label stay stuck on 'All'. Repair the output-utility filter so its tab row wraps and stays within the mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, the utility chips are legible with proper spacing and contrast, and clicking a category moves the active-tab highlight and updates the 'Showing N of M utilities · <category>' readout to reflect the chosen category and its live count. Keep the two-pane editor/translator layout, the SetConfig popover, the theme toggle, the Copy buttons, the SVG icons and the /css-to-tailwind basePath exactly as they are.
required_content: The output pane shows a native 'Filter utilities' tab row with the five categories All / Layout / Spacing / Color / Effects above the converted 'Out Code' rules on desktop, tablet and mobile.
A live 'Showing N of M utilities · <category>' readout sits with the filter tabs and reflects the currently selected category and the number of visible utility chips.
Clicking a category tab (for example Spacing) moves the active-tab highlight onto that tab and filters the emitted utility chips to that category, updating the readout to that category and count.

On a 390px mobile viewport the filter tab row and the whole converter page render with no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance; the fixed non-wrapping tab row must no longer force a horizontal scrollbar.
The emitted utility chips are legible with adequate spacing and colour contrast (no overlapping, clipped, or near-invisible dark-on-dark chips) on every viewport.

The two-pane layout (CSS editor + 'Out Code' translator), the SetConfig popover, the light/dark theme toggle, the per-rule Copy buttons, the GitHub link and the /css-to-tailwind basePath all remain reachable and functional; no console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
design_constraints: Preserve the tool's visual language: neutral light/dark surfaces, rounded pill controls, the 'Out Code' heading, and the green monospace result-code chips.
Do not remove or rename the filter categories or any workspace control; this is a repair of the filter's layout and state wiring, not a redesign.
The repair must live in the output-filter component and its stylesheet (components/OutputFilter.tsx, components/output-filter.css); the surrounding workspace, editor and popover stay unchanged.
The tab row must wrap / flex down responsively instead of holding a fixed non-wrapping width; tabs keep a sensible minimum but never exceed the mobile viewport.
The active-tab highlight and the 'Showing N of M utilities · <category>' readout must be driven by the live selected category, not a value captured once at first render.
Keep the console clean and avoid new network requests; do not introduce remote fonts, analytics, or CDN dependencies.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the converter workspace at 1440px: the CSS editor, the 'Out Code' translator with the converted rules, and the native 'Filter utilities' tab row with the 'Showing 30 of 30 utilities · All' readout, all within the viewport.
tablet_initial captures the same workspace at 834px.
mobile_initial captures the workspace at 390px, where the broken fixed-width tab row forces horizontal overflow; the repaired filter must wrap and stay within the viewport with legible chips.
desktop_spacing clicks the Spacing category tab: the active-tab highlight moves onto Spacing, the chips filter to spacing utilities, and the readout updates to 'Showing 6 of 30 utilities · Spacing'.
mobile_spacing clicks the Spacing tab at 390px and must also stay within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_config opens the SetConfig popover (prefix / useAllDefaultValues / customTheme) over the workspace.
desktop_light toggles the workspace into the light theme.
desktop_result_scroll scrolls the translator output list.

change_completion: The output pane renders the native 'Filter utilities' tab row (All / Layout / Spacing / Color / Effects) with a live 'Showing N of M utilities' readout above the converted 'Out Code' rules.
Clicking a category tab moves the active-tab highlight onto that tab, filters the emitted utility chips to that category, and updates the readout label and count to the chosen category.
design_consistency: The filter reuses the tool's rounded pill controls, dark/light surfaces, the 'Out Code' heading, and the green monospace result-code chip styling with no new palette or typography.
The utility chips are legible with adequate spacing and colour contrast — no overlapping, clipped, or near-invisible dark-on-dark chips on any viewport.
responsive: On a 390px mobile viewport the filter tab row wraps and the whole converter page renders with no horizontal overflow beyond a 24px tolerance.
The tab row flexes down responsively across desktop (1440px), tablet (834px) and mobile (390px) instead of holding a fixed non-wrapping width, both before and after a category is selected.
regression: The two-pane editor/translator layout, the SetConfig popover, the light/dark theme toggle, the per-rule Copy buttons, the GitHub link and the /css-to-tailwind basePath all remain reachable and functional.
No console errors or failed network requests are introduced and no remote fonts/analytics/CDN dependencies are added.
